input.message:
Dear Landlord,

Property: Flat 29, 19 Copperfield Walk, Northbridge, ZZ9 1ZZ
Reference: R/PM039-1 (Job ID NBL-039-2915)

Your tenant has reported that the washing machine makes a mechanical clicking noise while the drum rotates during washes. It is still working at the moment. We asked the tenant to check nothing loose in the drum was causing it, and they have confirmed it is a mechanical clicking from the machine itself. They have offered a video, which we will pass to the engineer.

Proposed fix: send an appliance engineer to inspect and diagnose the fault. We don't have a cost yet; if the engineer finds a repair is needed, we will come back to you with the quote before any repair work goes ahead.

Please reply APPROVE for us to arrange the inspection, or DECLINE if you would prefer otherwise. If you have a preferred engineer, or the machine is under warranty or cover, please let us know.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance Team

input.body:
Hi Nora,

Thank you for confirming. Yes please, a short video of the clicking noise during a wash would really help the engineer – just reply to this email with it attached.

We have asked the landlord to approve an engineer coming to inspect the machine. We'll update you within 3 working days, or sooner if we hear back. In the meantime you can keep using the machine. If the noise gets much worse, or you notice burning smells, smoke or leaking, stop the machine, switch it off at the wall and let us know straight away.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance Team

result.summary: The tenant's reply (event 006) answered the agency's question: the noise is a mechanical clicking from the machine and nothing suggests loose items, so the agent's condition for sending someone out is met. There is no landlord approval or spend limit on record, so I emailed the landlord asking for approval of an engineer inspection with no cost stated. I replied to the tenant to accept the video they offered and explain what happens next, and placed a 3-day hold to chase the landlord.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 003 said someone would be sent if nothing was inside the machine. Event 006 describes a mechanical clicking from the machine, which plausibly answers that question, so I took it at face value. Event 003 says the landlord was 'let know', but no approval and no pre-approved limit are recorded. Committing money without approval is not allowed, so I asked the landlord. Event 005 asked whether the tenant needs a reply. They do: they offered a video, and they need to know the next step and when they'll hear back.
